Yeah, we've barely scratched the surface of our ocean. According to the NOAA we've explored less than 5% of what is down there which is crazy in my opinion.

Because space is awesome. And so are lasers.

On a more serious note:

Firstly, there isn't much left to explore on earth that would really blow your mind.

Secondly, a pretty damn good reason to let your games play in space is the almost absolute freedom you have then. Having a game play on earth always puts a limit to what you can do without contradicting what we already know. Sure, you are free contradict in whatever way you want, but it's a fine line between creating a parallel universe and bullshitting your way through writing.

In space, the audio-, graphics- and game-designers have just as much freedom as the writers. A green sky on a sunny day? Bullshit if your game plays on earth, no problem if your game plays on a different planet in a different solar system or galaxy. It's the huge amount of explaining you don't have to do.

Deep sea is similar. While it isn't fully explored yet (not even close to be honest), we're still having a fairly good idea how life looks down there. (hint: absolutely fucking terrifying)

It stikes a good middle-ground. Besides that, the deep sea is the only place that matches the endless space in terms of oppressiveness. Claustrophobic, hostile and what little we know about it, is absolutely terrifying.
